cases.title: SecureCompany's office Wi-Fi
cases.explanation: Company SecureCompany adopted RFC 9704: its zone zivkovic.me is DNSSEC-signed at Cloudflare and publishes a Verification Record authorising dns.splittrust.zivkovic.me for internal.splittrust.zivkovic.me. SecureCompany's devices verify the office network's claim against the real DNS before using the office resolver for those names.

cases.title: Hotel Wi-Fi claims SecureCompany's domain
cases.explanation: A hotel network claims all of zivkovic.me and its resolver serves a forged copy of the zone: every name points at the hotel's page and the Verification Record carries the correct token for the hotel's claim. SecureCompany's device validates against the real DNSSEC chain (root, .me, Cloudflare) and rejects the claim; the hotel cannot produce Cloudflare's signatures.

cases.title: Hotel replays SecureCompany's claim
cases.explanation: The hotel copies SecureCompany's real claim word for word and announces its own resolver under SecureCompany's resolver name. The certificate is for dns.hotel.lab, so TLS identity fails before any DNS query.

cases.title: Company network, authorised claims
cases.exercises: RFC 9704 s5 token, s6.2 Secure, s7 ds binding (claim 1) and token-only authority (claim 2)
cases.explanation: corp.lab is signed and publishes Verification Records for dns.corp.lab (internal, with a ds key binding) and dns2.corp.lab (mail, token-only). Both claims are accepted; only the first one establishes local DNSSEC.

cases.title: Company network, authorised claims
cases.exercises: RFC 9704 s5 token, s6.2 Secure, s7 ds binding (claim 1) and token-only authority (claim 2)
cases.explanation: corp.lab is signed and publishes Verification Records for dns.corp.lab (internal, with a ds key binding) and dns2.corp.lab (mail, token-only). Both claims are accepted; only the first one establishes local DNSSEC.

cases.title: Hotel claims the bank (honest relay)
cases.exercises: s6.2 authenticated denial relayed by the hostile network -> RECORD_MISSING
cases.explanation: The hotel announces dns.hotel.lab as authoritative for all of banka.lab. Its resolver overrides www.banka.lab but relays everything else. The bank never published a record: the signed denial comes back through the hotel and the claim is rejected.

cases.title: Hotel claims the bank (honest relay)
cases.exercises: s6.2 authenticated denial relayed by the hostile network -> RECORD_MISSING
cases.explanation: The hotel announces dns.hotel.lab as authoritative for all of banka.lab. Its resolver overrides www.banka.lab but relays everything else. The bank never published a record: the signed denial comes back through the hotel and the claim is rejected.

cases.title: Hotel forges the Verification Record
cases.exercises: s6.2 Bogus: correct token in a record the parent zone never signed
cases.explanation: Same claim, but the hotel resolver now serves its own banka.lab view including dns.hotel.lab._splitdns-challenge.banka.lab TXT with the correct token. The token matches; the signature chain says the bank never signed it. Bogus, rejected.

cases.title: Claim changed before the record
cases.exercises: s11 ordering: record must change before the claim -> TOKEN_MISMATCH
cases.explanation: IT changed the salt in the announced claim but the zone still carries the record for the old salt. Expected token differs from the published one.

cases.title: Zone signatures expired
cases.explanation: expired.lab is signed, but its RRSIGs expired an hour ago. The record is Bogus and the claim is rejected.

cases.title: Unsigned parent zone
cases.exercises: s6.2 Insecure -> fail without policy; s6.1 external path for devices that have one
cases.explanation: unsigned.lab publishes a correct record but is not DNSSEC-signed. A validating device has no fallback and rejects; a device whose default resolver is an external encrypted resolver verifies through it (RFC 9704 section 6.1) and accepts, with its security resting on that resolver.

cases.title: Wrong ds key binding
cases.exercises: s7: ds RDATA must equal a DS computed over resolver.arpa. for a presented DNSKEY
cases.explanation: wrongds.lab publishes a record whose token matches but whose ds value does not correspond to the DNSKEY the resolver presents for resolver.arpa. Rejected.

cases.title: Hotel replays the company's claim
cases.exercises: s5: resolver must present a certificate for the claimed ADN (RFC 9525)
cases.explanation: The hotel copies corp.lab's real claim and announces its own resolver under the name dns.corp.lab. The record exists and the token matches, but the resolver cannot present a certificate for dns.corp.lab.

cases.title: Hotel blocks the external resolver
cases.exercises: s6.1: no response from the external resolver -> verification failed
cases.explanation: A device whose default resolver is quad9.lab tries to verify the hotel's claim through it, but the hotel blocks encrypted DNS egress. RFC 9704 section 6.1: no response means verification failed. The hotel gains only denial of service.

cases.title: Claim for a Special-Use name
cases.exercises: s3: Special-Use Domain Names MUST NOT be validated
cases.explanation: A network claims home.arpa. RFC 9704 section 3: Special-Use Domain Names MUST NOT be validated. Rejected without any network traffic.

description: Expected verdicts of the SplitTrust lab scenarios per simulated device. trust_context is always "lab": a private root, not the global DNS.

devices.hybrid: validating-stub that retries through the external resolver on Insecure
devices.private-dns: external encrypted resolver by default; RFC 9704 section 6.1
devices.validating-stub: validates DNSSEC locally, network resolver as DoT forwarder, no external policy
